summary_text:
Infrasub System (Audio)
New direction: infrasub (low-frequency extension) to be added to audio system
Described as an array of ~32 giant subwoofers, each roughly refrigerator-sized
Believed to be in HoloPlot’s Concept Plus presentation; not confirmed in Vanguardia model
Not yet a commercial product, still in development
Tom/Brennan to add to radar and get more detail from Derek
Drum Roof and Floor Level Options
Three options reviewed to avoid fireproofing the drum roof:
Raise structure only (more space, increases volume slightly)
Split-the-difference hybrid: raise roof ~4 ft, lower staff/donut level ~3 ft
Lower mechanical floor more aggressively (rejected: encroaches on IMS access)
Leading option is the hybrid (option 2)
Level 5 drops from ~20 ft floor-to-floor to ~17 ft
Large inflated duct behind IMS would need to shift; may split into two or work with fabric duct vendor on shape
Level 6 (donut level) actually benefits mechanically: larger systems run overhead there
MER Access Floor and Slab Drop
MER slab drop assumed at ~24 inches total
Raised access floor assembly: ~4–6 inches thick
Leaves ~18–20 inches clear underneath
Mechanical team needs ~16 inches clear for chilled water piping and in-row CRAC unit elbows
Extra clearance could also accommodate low-voltage runs (hybrid overhead/underfloor)
Preprogramming Room (Immersive Mix Room) Height Conflict
Room currently at Level 5 (top of bowl/concourse level); 17.5 ft clear today
Dropping staff level 3 ft reduces clear height to ~14–14.5 ft
Room requires ~3 m (~10 ft) clear from listening height; current setup already constrained
Room function: mini immersive audio dome (20+ speaker positions) to simulate bowl experience for show programming
Operator must be equidistant from all speakers; tallest point needed at center of space
Options discussed:
Relocate room to floor below (~27 ft clear, but mechanical congestion)
Localized structural modification to raise ceiling only in that zone
Electrical room swap (Exosphere electrical room between Quads A/B) may free adjacent space
TVS to cut a cross-section of the room showing current beam heights and post-modification heights (before and after)
Brandon to socialize the section; thread to include structural lead (Sturm) for commitment on feasibility
Floor above is office space; may be able to pop that zone up if needed
Programming comments from Vegas already driving some modifications to this area; TVS will incorporate
CUP Building: Layout and Utility Switches
Updated programming plans (with revised layouts) to be issued Friday
Three utility switches relocated outside CUP:
~8 ft × 8 ft pads, 3 ft clearance between, 10 ft clearance east and west
Placed behind screen wall for access and concealment
Daikin modular chiller pods: 4 ft hard clearance required off electrical panel side
Electrical panel orientation can be adjusted to maximize clearance; stair tower can tuck on opposite side
Third utility switch requires a new space within the main electrical room (two existing switches get resized); electrical team reviewing impact
Kyle raised possibility of reducing from 3 circuits to 2 with Pepco via metering data
Only viable if 14.5 kV load reduced; ME Engineers working on scheme, to share with Kyle this week
CUP Level 2 Access and Servicing Strategy
Boiler space at Level 2 needs a defined access/egress strategy for equipment servicing
Options: double doors with lift, telehandler, other method
To be resolved in detail at next week’s in-person meetings
Kyle flagged this as a key concern; will be a major agenda item next week
Underground Utilities and Drainage Scope
Underground utility routing (CUP to main Sphere building) underway
Primary item: duct bank from main electrical service; ME Engineers picking up at the three utility switches
Routing from south end of site up to switches, then into electrical room at CUP
Medium voltage underground to main electrical rooms at Level 1 of Sphere; ME Engineers to model this week
Coordination required around geopiles and caisson piles to minimize bends
Scope clarification on sub-slab drainage:
Buro Happold: waterproofing membrane recommendations only (vapor barrier or waterproofing per geotech criteria)
Geotech report: dictates drainage strategy; geotech firm typically also designs foundation drain and sub-slab drainage system
ME Engineers: designing sump pits to receive drainage, not the drainage system itself
Scope gap identified: third party (likely geotech) needs to be formally appointed to design the drainage system
Storm and hydronic routing partially in model from Concept Plus; to be revisited now that CUP shifted west
Model Coordination and Next Steps
TVS issued first Revit model recreation last Friday; finalizing interior spaces by this Friday
Transition from Manica architectural model to TVS architectural model to begin end of this week
ME Engineers advised to wait until early next week before merging TVS model with theirs
TVS to send email to all consultants when model is ready to link
Collective Revit upgrade to 2026 planned for near future via ACC platform (to avoid version obsolescence)
Next weekly coordination meeting: in-person at ME Engineers’ office next Tuesday, also virtual
Key agenda item: CUP Level 2 equipment access strategy
Updated programming plans to be reviewed in person
Darren visiting next week; AV/LV team to break off for separate powwow on AV-specific updates (Disguise, disguise, playout, etc.)
Meeting minutes to be sent later today or first thing tomorrow
All meeting minutes and agendas to include the specific Sphere address on distribution
Next Steps
Issue cross-section of preprogramming room with beam heights (Brandon)
Show current clear heights and post-modification heights (before and after staff level drop) to determine if room remains viable or needs to relocate.
Start thread with structural lead (Sturm) on localized ceiling modification
Explore raising ceiling only in the preprogramming room zone to resolve height conflict without relocating the room.
Share utility switch distribution scheme with Kyle this week (ME Engineers)
Working on 3-circuit accommodation scheme; Kyle to review load distribution and advise on Pepco negotiation feasibility.
Formally appoint geotech to design sub-slab drainage system
Scope gap confirmed: Buro Happold covers waterproofing only; geotech firm to design foundation drain and sub-slab drainage.
Model conduit routing (CUP to Sphere) in 3D this week (Art / ME Engineers)
Route from south end of site through utility switches into CUP electrical room, then to Level 1 main electrical rooms; coordinate around geopiles.
Send email to consultants when TVS model is ready to link (TVS)
ME Engineers to hold off merging until early next week; collective Revit 2026 upgrade to follow via ACC.
Add infrasub system to project radar and get specs from Derek (Tom / Brennan)
32-unit array not yet in Vanguardia model; confirm scope and facility impact for both HoloPlot and Vanguardia sides.
summary_markdown:
# Infrasub System (Audio)

- New direction: infrasub (low-frequency extension) to be added to audio system
  - Described as an array of \~32 giant subwoofers, each roughly refrigerator-sized
  - Believed to be in HoloPlot’s Concept Plus presentation; not confirmed in Vanguardia model
  - Not yet a commercial product, still in development
- Tom/Brennan to add to radar and get more detail from Derek

# Drum Roof and Floor Level Options

- Three options reviewed to avoid fireproofing the drum roof:
  1. Raise structure only (more space, increases volume slightly)
  2. Split-the-difference hybrid: raise roof \~4 ft, lower staff/donut level \~3 ft
  3. Lower mechanical floor more aggressively (rejected: encroaches on IMS access)
- Leading option is the hybrid (option 2)
  - Level 5 drops from \~20 ft floor-to-floor to \~17 ft
  - Large inflated duct behind IMS would need to shift; may split into two or work with fabric duct vendor on shape
  - Level 6 (donut level) actually benefits mechanically: larger systems run overhead there

# MER Access Floor and Slab Drop

- MER slab drop assumed at \~24 inches total
  - Raised access floor assembly: \~4–6 inches thick
  - Leaves \~18–20 inches clear underneath
- Mechanical team needs \~16 inches clear for chilled water piping and in-row CRAC unit elbows
- Extra clearance could also accommodate low-voltage runs (hybrid overhead/underfloor)

# Preprogramming Room (Immersive Mix Room) Height Conflict

- Room currently at Level 5 (top of bowl/concourse level); 17.5 ft clear today
  - Dropping staff level 3 ft reduces clear height to \~14–14.5 ft
  - Room requires \~3 m (\~10 ft) clear from listening height; current setup already constrained
- Room function: mini immersive audio dome (20+ speaker positions) to simulate bowl experience for show programming
  - Operator must be equidistant from all speakers; tallest point needed at center of space
- Options discussed:
  - Relocate room to floor below (\~27 ft clear, but mechanical congestion)
  - Localized structural modification to raise ceiling only in that zone
  - Electrical room swap (Exosphere electrical room between Quads A/B) may free adjacent space
- TVS to cut a cross-section of the room showing current beam heights and post-modification heights (before and after)
- Brandon to socialize the section; thread to include structural lead (Sturm) for commitment on feasibility
- Floor above is office space; may be able to pop that zone up if needed
- Programming comments from Vegas already driving some modifications to this area; TVS will incorporate

# CUP Building: Layout and Utility Switches

- Updated programming plans (with revised layouts) to be issued Friday
- Three utility switches relocated outside CUP:
  - \~8 ft × 8 ft pads, 3 ft clearance between, 10 ft clearance east and west
  - Placed behind screen wall for access and concealment
  - Daikin modular chiller pods: 4 ft hard clearance required off electrical panel side
  - Electrical panel orientation can be adjusted to maximize clearance; stair tower can tuck on opposite side
- Third utility switch requires a new space within the main electrical room (two existing switches get resized); electrical team reviewing impact
- Kyle raised possibility of reducing from 3 circuits to 2 with Pepco via metering data
  - Only viable if 14.5 kV load reduced; ME Engineers working on scheme, to share with Kyle this week

# CUP Level 2 Access and Servicing Strategy

- Boiler space at Level 2 needs a defined access/egress strategy for equipment servicing
  - Options: double doors with lift, telehandler, other method
  - To be resolved in detail at next week’s in-person meetings
- Kyle flagged this as a key concern; will be a major agenda item next week

# Underground Utilities and Drainage Scope

- Underground utility routing (CUP to main Sphere building) underway
  - Primary item: duct bank from main electrical service; ME Engineers picking up at the three utility switches
  - Routing from south end of site up to switches, then into electrical room at CUP
  - Medium voltage underground to main electrical rooms at Level 1 of Sphere; ME Engineers to model this week
- Coordination required around geopiles and caisson piles to minimize bends
- Scope clarification on sub-slab drainage:
  - Buro Happold: waterproofing membrane recommendations only (vapor barrier or waterproofing per geotech criteria)
  - Geotech report: dictates drainage strategy; geotech firm typically also designs foundation drain and sub-slab drainage system
  - ME Engineers: designing sump pits to receive drainage, not the drainage system itself
  - Scope gap identified: third party (likely geotech) needs to be formally appointed to design the drainage system
- Storm and hydronic routing partially in model from Concept Plus; to be revisited now that CUP shifted west

# Model Coordination and Next Steps

- TVS issued first Revit model recreation last Friday; finalizing interior spaces by this Friday
  - Transition from Manica architectural model to TVS architectural model to begin end of this week
  - ME Engineers advised to wait until early next week before merging TVS model with theirs
  - TVS to send email to all consultants when model is ready to link
- Collective Revit upgrade to 2026 planned for near future via ACC platform (to avoid version obsolescence)
- Next weekly coordination meeting: in-person at ME Engineers’ office next Tuesday, also virtual
  - Key agenda item: CUP Level 2 equipment access strategy
  - Updated programming plans to be reviewed in person
  - Darren visiting next week; AV/LV team to break off for separate powwow on AV-specific updates (Disguise, disguise, playout, etc.)
- Meeting minutes to be sent later today or first thing tomorrow
- All meeting minutes and agendas to include the specific Sphere address on distribution

# Next Steps

- **Issue cross-section of preprogramming room with beam heights** (Brandon)

  Show current clear heights and post-modification heights (before and after staff level drop) to determine if room remains viable or needs to relocate.
- **Start thread with structural lead (Sturm) on localized ceiling modification**

  Explore raising ceiling only in the preprogramming room zone to resolve height conflict without relocating the room.
- **Share utility switch distribution scheme with Kyle this week** (ME Engineers)

  Working on 3-circuit accommodation scheme; Kyle to review load distribution and advise on Pepco negotiation feasibility.
- **Formally appoint geotech to design sub-slab drainage system**

  Scope gap confirmed: Buro Happold covers waterproofing only; geotech firm to design foundation drain and sub-slab drainage.
- **Model conduit routing (CUP to Sphere) in 3D this week** (Art / ME Engineers)

  Route from south end of site through utility switches into CUP electrical room, then to Level 1 main electrical rooms; coordinate around geopiles.
- **Send email to consultants when TVS model is ready to link** (TVS)

  ME Engineers to hold off merging until early next week; collective Revit 2026 upgrade to follow via ACC.
- **Add infrasub system to project radar and get specs from Derek** (Tom / Brennan)

  32-unit array not yet in Vanguardia model; confirm scope and facility impact for both HoloPlot and Vanguardia sides.
